articles.excerpt: STATERA Library · Series 07 · Volume 02 · Chapter 02 · EN https://github.com/Statera-Library/07_Vol_02_Wire_Harness_Engineering/blob/main/Chapter_02_Current_Capacity/Chapter_02_Current_Capacity_EN.md…
articles.body: STATERA Library · Series 07 · Volume 02 · Chapter 02 · EN Source: https://github.com/Statera-Library/07_Vol_02_Wire_Harness_Engineering/blob/main/Chapter_02_Current_Capacity/Chapter_02_Current_Capacity_EN.md Volume 02. Wire Harness Engineering Chapter 02. Current Capacity 02.01. Continuous vs Transient Current Continuous current is the electrical current that a wire or conductor must carry for an extended period while the system remains in a normal operating state. In wire-harness engineering, its allowable value is primarily limited by thermal equilibrium. Electrical resistance produces heat according to I²R loss, while the conductor, insulation, terminals, and surrounding environment continuously dissipate that heat.

AI code agents produce output at a pace that makes manual review impractical. A Claude Code session can edit fifty files before the first test runs. The code lands in the repository clean or broken depending on whether validation happened before the commit. Most teams discover this after the damage shows up in CI. The problem sits between the agent's tool execution and the repository state. Claude writes code that passes its internal checks but fails the toolchain's stricter rules. Type errors appear that TypeScript would have caught. Tests break that were passing ten minutes earlier.

articles.body: STATERA Library · Series 07 · Volume 02 · Chapter 01 · EN Source: https://github.com/Statera-Library/07_Vol_02_Wire_Harness_Engineering/blob/main/Chapter_01_Wire_Physics/Chapter_01_Wire_Physics_EN.md Volume 02. Wire Harness Engineering Chapter 01. Wire Physics 01.01. Resistivity and Temperature Coefficient Electrical resistivity describes the intrinsic opposition of a conductor material to the movement of electric charge. Unlike resistance, which depends on the physical dimensions of a wire, resistivity is primarily a material property. For a uniform conductor, resistance is expressed as R = ρL/A, where ρ is resistivity, L is conductor length, and A is cross-sectional area.

articles.title: The hard part of an AI tutor is the reply students never should have seen
articles.excerpt: The failure I worried about was never "the tutor could not answer". It was the tutor answering confidently and wrongly, in front of a child who had no reason to doubt it. I work on an AI tutor used by…
articles.body: The failure I worried about was never "the tutor could not answer". It was the tutor answering confidently and wrongly, in front of a child who had no reason to doubt it. I work on an AI tutor used by students, and the asymmetry is uncomfortable. A model that says "I don't know" is a small disappointment. A model that states a wrong fact, drifts into an unsuitable topic, or phrases something in a way that reads badly to a younger student is a different category of problem, and you usually find out after the reply is already on screen. Reviewing a log at the end of the week does not help the student who read it on Tuesday. That is why the review has to sit before the student, not after. Why a blacklist was not enough My first instinct was a word filter. It lasted about an afternoon.
articles.author: LXSAIHUB

articles.title: Decompiling a Blazor WebAssembly App: Reading the .NET DLLs the Browser Downloaded
articles.excerpt: The first time someone opens the browser dev tools on a Blazor WebAssembly app and sees a _framework folder full of .wasm files, it looks reassuringly opaque — like the compiled WebAssembly blob you c…
articles.body: The first time someone opens the browser dev tools on a Blazor WebAssembly app and sees a _framework folder full of .wasm files, it looks reassuringly opaque — like the compiled WebAssembly blob you cannot read. It is not. Blazor WebAssembly does not compile your C# to WebAssembly; it ships a .NET runtime (as WASM) plus your ordinary .NET assemblies , and runs them in the browser. Those assemblies are downloaded to every visitor, metadata and IL intact, which means your client-side C# decompiles as cleanly as any DLL on your disk. Understanding how to read them is also the fastest way to understand what you must not put in them.
articles.author: Zero Heartbeat

articles.body: SpaceX is one big step closer to the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket. The company announced today (Nov. 10) that it had moved its latest Starship first stage, known as Super Heavy Booster 22, to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas ahead of Flight 15, which is scheduled to lift off this Friday (Nov. 13). During the upcoming launch test, SpaceX plans to catch both Booster 22 and Starship's Ship upper stage with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms in a double landing catch — something the private spaceflight company has never tried before. articles.excerpt: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday ad…
articles.body: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month’s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws — including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook — and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe , Apple , Google and Mozilla . Image: Shutterstock.com. Diorama by @zepp1969. November’s patch release from Redmond tackles 1,093 vulnerabilities, fixing 63 “critical” flaws that can be exploited to seize control over a Windows system with little or no help from users. Nearly half of those critical bugs are remote code execution vulnerabilities.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected.

articles.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
articles.excerpt: Researcher finds 35,000 Grok Build apps wide open to anyone who looked for them.
articles.body: Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data—some of it proprietary business information and other sensitive secrets—from thousands of its users, including the very same Elon Musk-owned company that offers the platform, new research shows. The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. Except in rare cases, clicking those links opens the app and reveals all data associated with it.
